name: Carolingian Westwork and Civitas Corvey
description: Beside the Weser River near Höxter in Germany stands the Westwork of Corvey, a massive tower-like church façade built in the 9th century. It is the only Carolingian structure still standing here, and the oldest of its kind. Inside, a vaulted hall with galleries holds rare wall paintings. Beyond it, the buried remains of the imperial abbey town lie only partly excavated.
